subject: Transient token-streaming anomaly — customer bulletin and follow-up
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@lumenware.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Transient token-streaming anomaly impacting short-batch responses

Samantha — good morning.

We wanted to alert you proactively that we observed a transient service deviation impacting a subset of hosted API requests this morning between 08:56 and 09:30 PDT. Symptoms included delayed streaming (partial token stalls) and elongated response times for short-generation requests typically under ~250 tokens. Your account (LumenWare) routed a measurable fraction of requests into the affected path; you may have noticed slower live responses for some sessions.

What we know so far:
- Impact window: ~08:56–09:30 PDT (we’ve included initial traces attached).
- Affected flows: streaming generation for small/low-token prompts and very short completions (conversational single-turn calls).
- Scope: ~3% of customer requests globally during the window; LumenWare saw higher concentration due to traffic pattern (many small bursts).

Immediate mitigations we applied:
- Automated routing to warmed inference pools for short-batch requests (reduced tail stalls within ~6 minutes of detection).
- Temporarily increased the minimal batching threshold for streaming to avoid pathological micro-batching that exposed a pacing bug.

Attachments: diag-logs-20280330.txt (sampling of traces), session-traces-lumenware-3-30.json (LumenWare request ids).

What we’re doing next:
- Full post-incident analysis (root cause, timeline, permanent fix) and a detailed follow-up by EOD.
- If you can share any additional request ids you saw impacted, please send them to ops@redwood.ai — we’ll prioritize correlating traces.

We apologize for the disruption. Thanks for your patience; we’ll follow up with a full summary and remediation plan shortly.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the heads up, Jordan.

We definitely saw an uptick in response times starting around 09:00 — several of our chat sessions stalled for a few seconds mid-response which caused timeouts on the client. Can you confirm:
1) Were any requests dropped or truncated?
2) Do you expect any replay/duplication risk if we retry failed calls?
3) ETA on full postmortem & whether this will qualify for SLA credit?

Appreciate the attachments; our infra team will send request ids if we find more.

— Samantha
Samantha Lee

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Mar 2028 10:05:43 -0700
Subject: Re: Transient token-streaming anomaly impacting short-batch responses

Jordan / Marissa — quick internal note and proposed customer-facing phrasing.

Summary of onboard findings (ops bridge):
- Root immediate trigger: a pacing regression in the streaming prefetch scheduler that, under high-frequency micro-bursts, could stall the token emission loop while waiting for an incentive threshold to batch.
- Why LumenWare saw more impact: their workload pattern spikes as many small single-turn requests; that pattern increased exposure to the prefetch path.
- No evidence of data loss or silent truncation. There were stalls; once the request resumed it completed normally. We saw a handful (~12) of requests that timed out client-side; those were not altered server-side (no duplication noted in traces).

Actions taken:
- Temporarily relaxed the batching threshold (mitigated within ~6 min).
- Ramp-block applied to the scheduler to prevent re-entering pathological state.
- Collected relevant traces + exported session ids (attached).

Next: full RCA + code-level fix scheduled today (owners: runtime-sched team). Recommend we offer LumenWare SLA credit for measurable client timeouts and include a detailed timeline.

Attaching: diag-logs-20280330.txt, session-traces-lumenware-3-30.json (for internal reference).

— Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Incident Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@lumenware.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, ops@lumenware.com
Date: Wed, 30 Mar 2028 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Follow-up: final incident summary and next steps — March 30, 2028 transient streaming anomaly

Samantha / LumenWare team — thank you again for flagging the impact and for sharing traces. Below is a concise post-incident summary and the remediation plan.

Incident timeline (UTC times for clarity):
- 15:56:24Z (08:56 PDT) — Monitoring alerts flagged elevated streaming stalls on short-batch requests. Automated detection triggered an ops bridge.
- 15:58:40Z — Rapid triage: identified regression in streaming prefetch scheduler.
- 16:04:12Z — Applied temporary routing to warmed pools + relaxed batching threshold (mitigation effective).
- 16:30:00Z — Service metrics returned to baseline for affected flows.
- 23:00:00Z — Post-incident verification completed; full trace export uploaded.

Root cause (summary):
A recent scheduler change introduced a batching incentive that, in extreme micro-burst patterns, delayed token emission while waiting to aggregate requests into a batch. This produced intermittent stalls for streaming responses on very short requests. The change was meant to reduce cost by promoting larger batches but had an unintended side-effect on emission pacing for small bursts.

Customer impact:
- Behavior observed: intermittent multi-second stalls during streaming; in a minority of cases the client timed out before the server resumed and completed the response.
- LumenWare specific: we saw ~0.7% of your requests experience client-visible timeouts within the window (~12 timed-out sessions identified). No data loss or corruption was observed.

Immediate mitigation & permanent fix: 
- Immediate: routing to warmed pools and relaxed batching threshold (already applied; reduced incidents within minutes).
- Short-term fix (today): patch to inhibit the batching incentive when sessions are categorized as low-token, high-frequency; deploy gated rollouts across regions.
- Long-term: scheduler rewrite to decouple emission pacing from batch-size incentive logic and improved workload classification heuristics.

Customer remediation & offer:
- We will credit LumenWare for customer-visible client timeouts that occurred during the window (we’ll follow up with exact credit amount and invoice application).
- We’ll share the full RCA doc and code change summary when the engineering postmortem is published (link below).

Attachments & artifacts:
- diag-logs-20280330.txt (sampled traces)
- session-traces-lumenware-3-30.json (your session ids — redacted where required)
- Postmortem doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/incident-2028-03-30
- Status entry: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2028-03-30-transient-token-streaming

Action items & owners:
- Runtime scheduler team: code patch and gated deploy (Ben Carter, owner) — ETA: 2028-03-30 EOD for rollout start, full verification by 2028-03-31.
- Customer reliability: finalize SLA credit calculation (Jordan Blake) — ETA: 2028-03-31 business day.
- Product/QA: add regression test cases to prevent reintroduction (Marissa Cole) — ETA: 2028-04-07.

If you’d like a short call to walk through the traces and the fix plan, I can arrange time this week with Ben and Marissa.

Again, sincere apologies for the disruption. We’re treating this as high priority and will share the engineered fix + postmortem once complete.

— Jordan
